samples.summary: `login` still bypasses the new single-classifier error contract (no envelope at all)
samples.evidence: The diff's new contract is stated absolutely — `packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:203` ("Every command that talks to the backend routes its `!res.ok` branch through here") and the reworked matrix in `docs/design/cli.md:1041-1057` / `packages/cli/README.md:116-126` ("Every command reports the same code for that condition, so the branch does not depend on which subcommand ran"). `packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts:62`, `:79` and `:96` each handle a failed backend response with `console.error('Token exchange failed. …')` / `console.error(\`Failed to fetch workspaces (HTTP ${wsRes.status})…\`)` followed by `process.exit(1)` — plain prose on stderr, no `{"error":{"code":…}}` envelope, no `HTTP_ERROR`. An agent branching on `error.code` gets nothing parseable from `wafflebase login`. Pre-existing code, but the diff is what promotes the claim to a documented invariant, so either login should route through the same helper or the docs should carve it out.

samples.summary: Image fetch failures during `docs export` / `slides export` still surface as code `ERROR`, not `HTTP_ERROR`
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:50-54` throws a plain `new Error(\`Image fetch failed: ${res.status} …\`)` on a non-ok upstream response. It is reached from `packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:249+` (pdf/docx export) and `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:197+` (pptx export) via `createImageFetcher`, inside the same try whose catch calls `outputError`. Because the thrown error carries no `code`, `errorCode()` (`packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:41-47`) falls back to `'ERROR'` — exactly the per-subcommand divergence the change advertises it has eliminated (README:122-126, docs/design/cli.md:1041-1057 say an upstream HTTP failure always reports `HTTP_ERROR`). Fix belongs on image-fetcher (throw an `UpstreamHttpError`) or on the doc wording.

samples.summary: `upstreamErrorJson` is applied to a branch that is not an HTTP failure, producing a misleading `HTTP 200` message
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/files/download.ts:56` guards `if (!res.ok || !res.bytes)`. The second disjunct fires on a *successful* response that carried no bytes; `upstreamErrorJson(res)` then formats `HTTP ${res.status}` from a 2xx status and emits `{"error":{"code":"HTTP_ERROR","message":"HTTP 200"}}`. The previous spelling printed `res.data ?? {error:{code:'HTTP_ERROR'}}`, which at least did not assert a bogus status. The helper's contract (`res` is a *failed* upstream response, formatter.ts:231-244) is not what this call site passes.

samples.summary: `UpstreamHttpError` is exported but never imported anywhere
samples.evidence: `export class UpstreamHttpError` (packages/cli/src/output/formatter.ts:187) has no importer: a repo-wide grep for `UpstreamHttpError` finds only its definition, doc comments (formatter.ts:182,214, docs/tasks/active/…-todo.md:24) — the new test file imports only `forwardUpstreamError`, `outputError` and `upstreamErrorJson`. knip runs over packages/cli with tests as entry points and fails on unused exports, so this is either a lane failure or a signal the class should not be exported.
